root_cause.text: The nat hook ops and their private data were freed immediately with kfree() without RCU grace period, creating a use-after-free race when the nfnl hook dump subsystem (added in v5.14) accesses these structures concurrently via the datapath's pointer-array blob.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces all kfree() calls on nat ops (nat_ops arrays and priv data) with kfree_rcu(). The commit message explicitly states that the nfnl hook dump code "will peek back into the nf_hook_ops that are available at the tail of the pointer-array blob used by the datapath" and that the nat hooks need to be deferred because they are called indirectly, indicating the need for RCU-safe freeing to avoid use-after-free.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces per-namespace dynamically allocated hook ops (kmemdup in ipt_nat_register_lookups) and frees them with kfree() in ipt_nat_unregister_lookups (line with 'kfree(ops)'). There is no RCU grace period before freeing, which can lead to use-after-free when the nfnl hook dump subsystem concurrently accesses the ops via the pointer-array blob. The code does not include any fix such as kfree_rcu or synchronize_rcu.
